title: atom_search is substring-only while bro_agent_search is vector-backed — sibling registries, asymmetric retrieval
wanted_capability: Retrieval parity (or an explicit decision against it) for the two manifest registries. bro_agent_search embeds queries against the AgentManifest bucket and resolves through the shared process-wide query cache (resolve_agent_vector_search); atom_search over the same kind of registry is field-substring matching only. Either atoms deserve the same vector lane (atom manifests are prose-rich — purpose/effects/contracts paraphrase poorly for substring match) or neither registry does and agent search's vector lane is over-engineering — but the asymmetry today is an accident of implementation order, not a decision. Surfaced by the 2026-06-12 corpus-search-surface scrutiny (one of four structural inconsistencies; the other three — parser fragmentation, project-scoping split, rerank divergence — were addressed by the taxonomy arc and the smart-mode/ranking work, leaving this one).
